topics.topic: Define the complete PERSONAL_DATA_FIELDS schema and how nested models, collections, and reused facts are identified and recursively classified
questions: What are the complete rows and exact field paths of `PERSONAL_DATA_FIELDS`, including nested objects, list items, import mappings and every other answer shape?

For nested models, list items and reused domain facts, which model and field must a pair name, and does classification recursively inspect nested values or classify only direct fields of the outer answer model?
When a classified fact is nested inside another answer field, which model and field identify it in the table, and must `operations` recursively inspect nested models and collections?

judgement.why: This asks the same State 6 schema, field-path, nested-value traversal and value-presence questions already judged in P15, and the relevant passage has not changed.

precedent.topic: Runtime value-presence and nested-field rules for answer disclosure classification
quotes:
`operations` computes an answer's class as the highest of its
  facts' — `personal_data` when one of those fields holds a value — and refuses the answer whole
  when it is above the caller's highest (A09 rule 4):
precedent.why: Runtime traversal of nested answer schemas and the representation and interpretation of optional or absent fields are State 6 contract, schema and field-type questions.

topics.topic: Define the machine-readable premature file-stream termination protocol and its owning module
questions: What exact result or exception does the stream owned by `upload_framing` expose so that `migration_import` can distinguish premature termination from normal end-of-part, and which contract owns that protocol?
Which module owns the machine-readable signal that distinguishes a normal end of the file part from premature end of the request, and what dependency lets `migration_import` recognize it?
What representation carries this framing failure from the stream owned by `upload_framing` through `operations` to `migration_import`, and which module owns that representation?

quotes:
`UploadBody`'s one implementation is
  `MultipartFileBody(stream, delimiter)`, `policy`, owned by
  `upload_framing`: it gives the file part's bytes and ends before the
  delimiter, holding in memory no more than the delimiter's length of
  look-ahead, so `_parse_export` still receives the bare JSON object. A
  stream that ends before the delimiter makes its `read` raise, a failure of
  the stream that `read_import_mapping` answers `file_unreadable`, as any
  stream that fails; a request that declares less than the head and the
  delimiter answers an `UploadHead` with none of its values.
judgement.why: The later contract makes MultipartFileBody the upload_framing-owned UploadBody implementation, uses a raised read failure as the machine-readable signal, and requires read_import_mapping to translate it to file_unreadable.

topics.topic: Define the Secure-cookie policy and policy owner for loopback HTTP
questions: Does Registry guarantee that the cookie is never transmitted over plain HTTP, or does it merely set the cookie's HTTPS-only attribute while allowing browser-specific loopback transmission over plain HTTP?
Must Registry mark the cookie `Secure` for loopback requests too, or may it issue a cookie usable over loopback HTTP; and which component chooses that policy?

quotes:
The session cookie
is always HTTPS-only (A13 rule 1, owner, 2026-11-17): from another machine
the interface is reached only through HTTPS (R0-29); whether a browser on
Registry's own machine sends it over plain HTTP to a loopback address is
that browser's, and where it does not, HTTPS there too is the host's
(Explicit exclusions).
judgement.why: The owner_interface ownership passage requires the cookie to be HTTPS-only for every origin while expressly leaving browser handling of that cookie on plain-HTTP loopback outside Registry's guarantee.

topics.topic: Define when null, absent, empty, and structurally empty values count as holding classified data
questions: Precisely when does a classified field hold a value: how are null, an explicit absent marker, an empty object, an empty list and a list containing only records without personal fields classified?

judgement.why: This is the same runtime value-presence and optional or absent-field interpretation question already assigned to State 6 by P15, and its governing passage has not changed.
